**How the survivors were classed.** This is the seat's call, and the session can veto it.

* **Q07 is not equivalent.** It removes the per-family binding of the cap, and no test pins that binding. The real code
  binds each family correctly. `support.ts:1339` reads `insertChainRefusalCap(op, runs)`, and the probe `zz-percap`
  above executed `verdict` for each of the seven operations at cap and cap + 1 (CONFIRMED). The survivor is therefore
  a missing meta-test (a further hardening test). It is not a wrong result, a missing interface or test id, or a red
  gate.
* **Q11 changes the measured baseline itself.** That is data owned by the session's ratchet (C-0231's table; "raising
  one is the session's call"), not a fault in the counting.
* **Q09 never reaches a different outcome on the drawn domain.** Probe `zz-setup.mts` ran 2 × 10⁴ offsetFace setups:
  19 994 were `ok`, 6 had no bounded face (settled either way) and 0 were refused with any code. Its direction is
  also stricter, since it counts more against the cap, never fewer.

Under N-45 (J202) and section (3) of the brief, the seat classes Q07, Q09 and Q11 as notes for the hardening pass,
not blockers. The brief's survivor rule ("a survivor on a stated promise you do not find equivalent stays a BLOCKER")
was weighed against N-45's owner-approved "a further hardening test is a KI row … never a fail". Q07 is the only
non-equivalent survivor on a stated promise. The seat holds that the promise itself (each family capped at its own
measured cap) is met by the real code and was confirmed by execution, so the gap is the missing pin only. A
one-loop test in `harness.test.ts` closes it (note 17). If the session reads the survivor rule as binding here, the
fix round is that loop alone.
